papers.title: Evaluating Bayesian deep learning for robust biomedical time-series classification under distribution shift: A sleep scoring case study
papers.summary: Evaluated Bayesian model averaging (BMA) from nine approximate inference methods across two neural network backbones for rodent sleep scoring under distribution shift in genotype, laboratory, and species. Multi-basin methods performed best, and BMA generally improved out-of-distribution accuracy, calibration, selective prediction, and artifact detection versus point estimates, while improving inter-rater disagreement detection little.

papers.title: Behavioral evidence for two-stage sleep in spiders.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: The study characterized sleep behavior in the jumping spider Portia fimbriata using behavioral and circadian analyses, demonstrating diurnal activity, a free-running circadian rhythm, robust sleep architecture, REM-like states with elevated arousal thresholds, and rebound effects after sleep disruption. The authors conclude that spiders exhibit behavioral sleep with an REM-like substate, providing evidence for such a state in a terrestrial invertebrate.

papers.title: Closed-Loop Acoustic Stimulation of Slow Oscillations Using a Wireless EEG Headband: A Polysomnography-Validated Feasibility Study.
papers.summary: Tested a real-time modeling-based closed-loop acoustic stimulation approach using a wireless forehead EEG headband in healthy participants during one night, with simultaneous PSG as reference. SO phase was targeted near the intended phase, and stimulation immediately enhanced SO dynamics plus sustained increases in SO density and delta/SO power (0.75-5 Hz) in both headband and PSG signals.

papers.title: Sleep Variables in Health Research: From Systematic Omission to Methodological Integration - A Narrative Review and Proposal.
authors: Adryel Luciano de Souza Matoso Alves
papers.summary: Argues that sleep variables are systematically omitted from baseline sample characterization in health and physiological research, producing residual confounding and a 'Table 1 Fallacy.' Proposes a high-yield, low-cost Minimal Sleep Set (MSS) using validated screening tools to control for sleep duration, quality, and circadian alignment as a methodological mandate.

papers.title: High-fat diet-induced MAFLD is associated with sleep architecture disruption via hippocampal neuroinflammation and bifurcated IRS-1/Akt/mTOR signaling in mice.
papers.summary: Male BALB/c mice fed a 60% high-fat diet for 16 weeks developed MAFLD with hepatic steatosis, systemic inflammation, hippocampal neuroinflammation, reduced NREM and REM sleep, sleep fragmentation, diminished NREM delta power, and a dampened circadian NREM delta rhythm, alongside increased hippocampal p-IRS-1 (Ser307), decreased p-Akt (Ser473), and elevated p-mTOR (Ser2448). The findings propose a liver-hippocampus-sleep axis linking MAFLD-driven inflammation and IRS-1/Akt/mTOR dysregulation to sleep disruption.

papers.title: Accurate EEG-based linear state-space model of cortical dynamics during a passive motor task with exogenous input.
papers.summary: Used subspace identification to fit linear time-invariant state-space models of EEG cortical dynamics during a passive motor task with continuous multisine wrist perturbations as exogenous input in seven participants. The linear models accurately represented the measurements in latent space, with constructed maps linking latent dynamics to neural source space and results aligning with prior studies.

papers.title: Automated Sleep Staging Performance Across Two Experimental Sleep Manipulation Protocols in Adolescents.
papers.summary: The study evaluated POPS, YASA, and combined POPS+YASA automated sleep staging against manual polysomnography in adolescents across sleep restriction and slow-wave sleep deprivation protocols, finding moderate-to-substantial agreement overall (Cohen's k 0.53-0.76). Agreement was lower under restricted versus extended sleep and declined across restriction nights, with poorer Wake/N1/N2 classification, while slow-wave sleep deprivation reduced overall agreement with poorer N3 classification.

papers.title: Sleep and Drowsiness in Cattle: A Narrative Review of Physiology, Measurement, and Methodological Challenges.
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: Narrative review of 22 primary studies synthesizing cattle NREM/REM sleep and drowsing physiology, measurement approaches (PSG, behavior, accelerometry, automated classification), and methodological limitations. Reported sleep and drowsing durations vary widely, drowsing overlaps with quiet wakefulness and light sleep, and evidence remains insufficient to establish causal links between sleep variation and cattle health, welfare, or performance.

papers.title: A Unified Flexible Large Polysomnography Model for Sleep Staging and Downstream Clinical Screening
papers.summary: Presents LPSGM, a large polysomnography model trained on 220,500 hours from 16 public datasets using domain-adaptive pretraining and flexible channel configurations. It achieved expert-level sleep staging (kappa 0.845 vs inter-expert 0.850) and supported downstream screening of narcolepsy (84.2% accuracy), severe OSA (AUC 0.874), and depression (AUC 0.801, cross-dataset 0.965).

papers.title: Characterising sleep spindle emergence in infancy: Effects of prematurity and early locomotor intervention
papers.summary: Daytime high-density EEG in 50 infants at 2 months corrected age (full-term, very preterm, and preterm with locomotor training) showed rhythmic sleep spindle organization roughly three times slower than in adults, with no group differences in temporal organization. Untrained preterm infants had more diffuse spindle-band activity than full-term infants, whereas trained preterm infants showed a spatial distribution resembling full-term infants but lower frontal spindle density.

papers.title: RefineSleepNet: Task-Driven Signal-Domain Transformation for EEG/EOG Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: Proposes RefineSleepNet, a sequence-to-sequence framework that separates task-driven signal refinement of EEG/EOG waveforms (SRU-Net) from epoch feature extraction, followed by fused sequence attention. In subject-independent 10-fold cross-validation it reached accuracy/macro-F1 of 84.5%/79.8% (Sleep-EDF-39), 83.5%/78.1% (Sleep-EDF-153), and 80.3%/78.1% (ISRUC-3).

papers.title: CSPT-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Framework Integrating Center-Driven Sequence Supervision and Multimodal Pyramid Token Encoding.
papers.summary: Proposes CSPT-SleepNet, integrating center-driven sequence supervision with multimodal pyramid token encoding for EEG/EOG/EMG sleep staging. Subject-independent cross-validation yielded accuracy/macro-F1 of 87.93%/83.53% (Sleep-EDF-20), 85.81%/80.87% (Sleep-EDF-78), and 84.06%/82.86% (ISRUC-S3), with N1 recognition remaining challenging.

papers.title: Ketones and Sleep: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Preclinical Models, and Human Evidence.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing mechanistic, preclinical, and human evidence on ketone bodies and sleep. It reports that AcAc (but not BHB) increases NREM slow-wave activity and suppresses glutamate release in mice, while human findings are suggestive but heterogeneous, with ketone effects on sleep conditional rather than universally sleep-promoting.

papers.title: Circadian patterns of device-detected postoperative atrial fibrillation during 2.5 years of continuous monitoring after cardiac surgery: The RACE V-Tissue Bank Study.
papers.summary: Continuously monitored 98 cardiac surgery patients for 2.5 years with implantable loop recorders to characterize circadian patterns of postoperative atrial fibrillation. New-onset POAF had a uniform 24-hour distribution whereas prior AF peaked in the morning; among 20 rhythmic patients, adrenergic, vagal, and mixed chronotypes were identified and linked to atrial remodeling markers and arrhythmia-related outcomes.

papers.title: Epithelial function of the circadian clock gene, Bmal1, in regulating the mucosa.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
papers.summary: Using a conditional knockout of the core clock gene Bmal1 in mouse colon epithelial cells, this study shows Bmal1 promotes colonic mucus production before injury, and its loss lowers mucus output, drives male-specific colitis exacerbation, and delays injury resolution in both sexes. The authors conclude that epithelial sex-specific clock rhythms are required for optimal colon barrier homeostasis.

papers.title: Effects of Circadian Phase and Exercise Training on Systemic and Tissue-Specific Redox Responses in Mice Fed a High-Fat Diet.
papers.summary: In high-fat-diet-fed male C57BL/6J mice, 8 weeks of treadmill training at ZT3 versus ZT15 was compared for systemic and tissue-specific redox responses; exercise increased plasma biological antioxidant potential irrespective of phase, while tissue redox-related transcriptional changes (e.g., soleus Hmox1, hepatic Keap1) were mainly circadian-phase-dependent and tissue-specific. The authors note that whether active-phase exercise confers a redox advantage requires further investigation.

papers.title: Indirect Skin Homeostasis Modulation by an Essential Oil Blend in Mice with Insomnia Comorbid Anxiety: Sensitivity of Dermal Fibroblasts to Exogenously Applied Circulating Molecules.
papers.summary: In a para-chlorophenylalanine-induced mouse model of insomnia comorbid anxiety, an essential oil blend (300 mg/kg intraperitoneal) alleviated anxiety- and insomnia-like behaviors, normalized brain neurotransmitters and hormones, and altered serum/skin cortisol, melatonin, 5-hydroxytryptamine, IL-10, and type I collagen; cultured dermal fibroblasts showed molecule-specific responses in oxidative stress, inflammation, and extracellular matrix synthesis. The authors caution that the in vitro assays show cellular sensitivity only and do not establish a causal brain-skin axis mechanism.

papers.title: Sex differences in sleep and memory relationships in older adults at risk for Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: In 80 cognitively unimpaired older adults enriched for Alzheimer's disease risk undergoing overnight polysomnography with high-density EEG (65 completing a word-pair memory task), overnight memory retention did not differ by sex, but exploratory analyses suggested sex-by-APOE ε4 interactions and sex-specific NREM sleep-memory associations (N2 duration in men; frontal slow and fronto-central fast sigma power in women). APOE-stratified analyses further indicated sex-specific sleep stage-memory relationships surviving FDR correction, supporting consideration of sex as a biological variable in sleep and cognitive aging research.

papers.title: Circadian aging and neurodegeneration: the emerging role of the melatonin-cortisol axis in brain homeostasis, disease progression, and precision chronomedicine.
papers.summary: This review proposes that circadian aging dysregulates the melatonin-cortisol axis—via reduced nighttime melatonin, blunted cortisol rhythms, abnormal clock-gene oscillations, and disrupted sleep-wake architecture—promoting oxidative stress, mitochondrial failure, neuroinflammation, and proteostasis failure linked to neurodegenerative disease. It discusses candidate biomarkers (endocrine, transcriptomic, multi-omics, wearable digital) and chronotherapeutic strategies including melatonin receptor agonists, bright-light therapy, time-restricted eating, exercise chronotherapy, sleep optimization, and microbiota modulation, while addressing inter-individual variability and trial-design challenges.

papers.title: Tablet-Camera Iris Landmarks and EEG/PPG-Derived Arousal Indices During Naturalistic Reading: Geometric Confounding and Exploratory Within-Subject Associations.
papers.summary: Evaluated whether MediaPipe iris landmark distances from a tablet camera estimate EEG/PPG-derived arousal during naturalistic reading across 43,923 thirty-second windows from 48 participants; raw iris distances correlated weakly with EEG alpha but face scale explained 93% of their variance, and after full adjustment for ocular luminance and head pose the alpha association was nonsignificant (r=+0.021).

papers.title: Interventional Effects and Neurometabolic Regulation of a Panax quinquefolius-Containing Herbal Extract (JYF) in Diazepam Withdrawal Syndrome in Mice.
papers.summary: Characterized a Panax quinquefolius-containing herbal extract (JYF) and tested it in a diazepam-withdrawal mouse model, finding that JYF attenuated withdrawal-associated weight loss, anxiety-like behavior, sleep fragmentation, and abnormal EEG activity, with metabolomic shifts in tryptophan and phenylalanine pathways and monoamine neurotransmitters moving toward control levels.

papers.title: Association of Total Atherosclerosis Burden of Baroreceptor-Resident Arteries with Heart Rate Variability and Its Circadian Rhythm in Patients with Ischemic Stroke.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 253 first-ever ischemic stroke patients, higher CTA-assessed total atherosclerosis burden of baroreceptor-resident arteries was nonlinearly associated with lower 24 h SDNN (1.67 ms decrease per 1-point increase) and reduced circadian SDNN amplitude in intermediate- and high-burden tertiles.

papers.title: Wearable-derived sleep and circadian features associated with electronic health record-documented persistent postsurgical pain.
papers.summary: Used longitudinal Fitbit and electronic health record data from the All of Us Research Program to show that patients later documented with persistent postsurgical pain had systematic shifts in wake timing and elevated heart rate circadian amplitude and mesor, with wake timing decoupled from heart rate circadian timing, absent in a comparison cohort without persistent pain.

papers.title: Effects of Maternal Caffeine Exposure During Gestation on Neurobehavior, Glucose Metabolism and Circadian Rhythm in Offspring Rats.
papers.summary: In pregnant Sprague-Dawley rats given caffeine (5, 20, 80 mg/kg/day) throughout gestation, offspring showed elevated spontaneous activity and anxiety-like behavior, impaired glucose tolerance specifically in females, and disrupted hepatic circadian clock-gene rhythmicity, while spatial learning/memory and insulin sensitivity were unaffected. High-dose caffeine also reduced maternal weight gain.

papers.title: Maternal sleep deprivation is associated with fetal hypothalamic-hepatic remodeling and long-term metabolic and behavioral alterations in offspring.
papers.summary: Using a mouse model of chronic gestational sleep deprivation, this study reports sex-dependent offspring outcomes: female MSD offspring showed delayed-onset glucose intolerance, insulin resistance, and altered lipid utilization with aging, while males showed mild changes; both showed altered anxiety/helplessness indices exacerbated by chronic stress. Transcriptomics indicated coordinated fetal hypothalamic-hepatic remodeling with persistent adult metabolic pathway dysregulation.

papers.title: Ozone as a Catalyst for Alzheimer's Disease and Sleep Disorders: Implications for Neurodegeneration Induced by Air Pollution.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing experimental and epidemiological evidence that tropospheric ozone generates a systemic oxidative-inflammatory signal affecting the CNS, with sleep/circadian disruption and Alzheimer's-related pathology as potentially reinforcing downstream outcomes; concludes ozone is a biologically plausible but not yet epidemiologically confirmed risk factor.

papers.title: Overt and Covert Speech-State Classification from Tripolar Concentric Ring Electrode EEG: A 4 mm and 10 mm Configuration Study.
papers.summary: Applied 4 mm and 10 mm tripolar concentric ring electrodes to record EEG during 200 picture-naming trials (100 overt, 100 covert) in 16 participants, comparing classification with LDA, SVM, and EEGNet. Overt speech produced higher task-to-baseline ratios than covert speech, and EEGNet achieved the highest mean accuracy (84.06±15.57%), followed by SVM (81.56±14.23%) and LDA (76.56±15.30%).

papers.title: Oxidative Stress in Pediatric Obstructive Sleep Apnea Syndrome: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: Narrative review summarizing mechanisms, biomarkers, and clinical consequences of oxidative stress in pediatric obstructive sleep apnea syndrome, including intermittent hypoxia-driven redox pathways (NADPH oxidases, HIF-1α, NF-κB, mitochondrial dysfunction, ER stress) and associated endothelial, cardiovascular, neurocognitive, and metabolic injury. It reports that oxidative and end-organ injury do not consistently parallel the apnea-hypopnea index and that methodological heterogeneity and lack of standardized pediatric reference values limit biomarker use.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis reveals that sleep deprivation exacerbates intestinal barrier injury via the microbiota-dependent taurodeoxycholic acid/group 3 innate lymphoid/IL-22 axis.
papers.summary: Used multi-omics (metagenomics, untargeted metabolomics, RNA sequencing) in a water-based mouse sleep deprivation model (0-96 h) plus germ-free mice, FMT, and flow cytometry to show prolonged sleep deprivation reshaped gut microbiota and suppressed microbial taurodeoxycholic acid (TDCA) metabolism, impairing barrier integrity via the TDCA/group 3 innate lymphoid cell/IL-22 axis. TDCA supplementation restored ILC3 function, IL-22 production, and barrier integrity.

papers.title: Menopausal Symptom Burden and Self-Reported Poor Sleep Quality Among Japanese Working Women Aged 40 Years and Older: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: Exploratory cross-sectional study of 79 Japanese working women aged 40 and older combining Simplified Menopausal Index scores, self-reported sleep quality, and wearable EEG-measured sleep duration. After adjusting for age and objective sleep duration, total and domain-specific menopausal symptom burden were associated with self-reported poor sleep quality, and associations persisted in sensitivity analyses excluding the sleep-related SMI item.

papers.title: Effects of 24-h sleep deprivation on circulating irisin, BDNF, and soluble klotho responses during exercise in the heat in young and older males.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
papers.summary: Randomized crossover study in 10 young and 10 older males comparing normal sleep versus 24-h total sleep deprivation before three 30-min cycling bouts in hot, dry conditions (40°C), measuring circulating irisin, BDNF, and soluble klotho. Older males had lower concentrations of all three biomarkers, and exercise in the heat increased irisin, but 24-h sleep deprivation did not detectably alter irisin, BDNF, or s-klotho responses in either age group.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances and Circadian Phase Delay in People Living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV): A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 15 studies found a high prevalence of poor sleep quality and delayed circadian phase in people living with HIV, with these chronobiological alterations linked to systemic inflammation, altered melatonin levels, impaired cognition, and metabolic changes involving leptin, ghrelin, adiponectin, and PPAR signaling. The authors noted an absence of clinical trials and proposed chronotherapeutic interventions plus sleep hygiene as complements to antiretroviral therapy.

papers.title: Exploratory Metabolomic and Metagenomic Profiling of Fecal Samples in Isolated REM Sleep Behavior Disorder.
papers.summary: In an exploratory cross-sectional multi-omics study of fecal samples from 21 isolated REM sleep behavior disorder patients and 15 controls, branched-chain fatty acids were selectively increased, volatile indole reduced, and the microbiome depleted of Blautia and Faecalibacterium; integrated host-microbe signatures discriminated patients from controls with 84.8% cross-validated accuracy.

papers.title: Early Post-Operative Quantitative EEG Central Beta Power Predicts Futile Recanalization After Endovascular Treatment in AIS-LVO.
papers.summary: In 56 acute ischemic stroke patients with large-vessel occlusion after successful endovascular treatment, higher central relative beta power on ~24-h postoperative QEEG was independently associated with lower 90-day futile recanalization (adjusted OR 0.28 per 1-SD increase), and adding it to a clinical model raised LOOCV AUC from 0.557 to 0.719.

papers.title: Effects of Sleep Deprivation on Oral Health: A Literature Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review describes mechanisms by which chronic sleep deprivation compromises oral health across five domains: immune dysregulation and periodontal destruction, salivary environment changes affecting caries and halitosis, behavioral mediators, neuromuscular consequences such as bruxism and temporomandibular dysfunction, and obstructive sleep apnea as an oral health comorbidity. It argues that sleep deprivation is an independent risk factor for oral conditions and outlines dental screening and referral practices.

papers.title: Seasonal Variation, Circadian Patterns, and Night Eating Syndrome Among Older Adults: The Mediating Role of Sleep Quality.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional path analysis of 336 community-dwelling older adults, sleep quality significantly mediated the associations of seasonal variation with circadian pattern (41% of the modeled association) and with night eating syndrome (37%), with 85.1% reporting poor sleep quality and 23.2% meeting criteria for full night eating syndrome.

papers.title: Depressive Symptoms, Insomnia-Related Difficulties and Self-Rated Health Among Community-Dwelling Adults Aged 40 Years and Older in Western China: A Cross-Sectional Structural Equation Modelling Study.
papers.summary: Structural equation modelling in 433 community-dwelling adults aged ≥40 in western China found an insomnia-derived construct had the largest direct association with self-rated health (β=0.383) and statistically mediated an indirect association between depressive symptoms and self-rated health (0.208).

papers.title: Correction: Physiological synchrony in heart rate and electrodermal activity predicts decreased vigilant attention induced by sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: Published erratum correcting the article on heart rate and electrodermal physiological synchrony predicting decreased vigilant attention induced by sleep deprivation. No new findings are reported in the correction notice.

papers.title: Assessment of night eating syndrome and circadian-related characteristics among university students of Rawalpindi and Islamabad.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional survey of 335 university students in Rawalpindi and Islamabad found a 6% prevalence of Night Eating Syndrome, with greater NES severity associated with lower Morningness and Good Sleep scores but not with Depressed Mood.

papers.title: Migraine burden and occupational impact among corporate employees attending neurology clinics in Skardu, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.
papers.journal: International journal of occupational safety and ergonomics : JOSE
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of corporate employees with neurologist-confirmed migraine in Skardu, Pakistan, reported high migraine burden (58.9±13.6) and substantial occupational impact, with high impact predicted by frequent attacks, stress, sleep deprivation, poor management and IT-sector employment.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
